about: The 49 rows of the rust-engine slice that trillion-workshop PR #133 found to be product features (workshop-tool or app-screen), not engine. Three already have a home byte for byte (src/delegation-ceilings.json and .mjs in tools/shared-code, src/optional-read.mjs in tools/find-and-keep-my-connections). Thirteen move here byte for byte, grouped by job folder. The rest are held: their import closures reach the Worker's engine owners (decision store, EEAF store, record log, sign-in, record-model tools) or call KV, which stays; each held group says so in held_until. src/resource-activity-projection.mjs is retired (it imports ./activity.mjs, absent at the tag), listed under retired.

not_provider_calls.why: placeCacheFolder(env = process.env) reads the cache folder a computer names in its process environment; it is no Worker binding.

groups.capability: run a customer database the account owns (PGlite), list its tables and attach it as a Workshop provider
fingerprint what a person consented to before an introduction, so a changed request is asked again
name the job slots a tool can fill, for finding the tool for a job
the caps on pursuit plans and work for AIs, and reading them
which model route each kind of call takes (its reader src/model-routes.mjs is held)
the rules a person sets for when stored bytes are released

groups.held_until: its own test at the tag (test/outbound-recipient.test.mjs) fails 3 of 5 against the code at the tag, and its fixtures carry phone numbers outside the 555 range that may be a real person's; the Workshop is public, so it waits for a synthetic test that passes

groups.capability: the own-records rows a pursuit reads (src/record-scope.mjs, its larger scope reader, is held)
readable names for shared and published things
